issues.body:
`_repo_confirmed_private` is added to ci-latency-alert.py, dispatch-stall-alert.py, groom-mint-alert.py, metrics-alert.py, park-stock-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py, but no file adds a single assertion against the helper itself.

Every new `--self-test` row passes an injected `lambda r, t: True|False` into `_alert_route`, which bypasses the real helper entirely. Consequently:

- In ci-latency-alert.py, dispatch-stall-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py the helper is NEVER executed by any self-test. dispatch-stall-alert.py's flow test pops ALERT_TOKEN (line 1096), so it takes the registry branch and never reaches the lookup.
- In groom-mint-alert.py, metrics-alert.py and park-stock-alert.py the added `fake_run` / `responses` entries stub only the happy path (`{"private": true}`), so the helper's happy branch runs and its four fail-closed branches do not.

Unasserted in all six copies: non-zero returncode -> False; unparseable/empty stdout -> False; `"private": false` -> False; a non-boolean `private` value -> False; and that the probe is a GET of `repos/{ALERT_REPO}` issued under the ROUTE token rather than the ambient one.

This is the repo's own bar, not a new one. Four sibling copies already in the tree pin exactly these five rows: groom-alert.py:385-398, plan-alert.py:580-593, usage-alert.py:896-911, worker-pr.py:11886-11902. Under the current tests a copy/paste slip - truthy `payload.get("private")` instead of `is True`, a dropped `returncode` guard, or the token argument not being threaded to `_gh` - would leave every row green while the route silently re-opened.
issues.fix_hint: Port the existing five-row block (groom-alert.py:373-398 is the closest template) into each of the six files, stubbing `_gh`/`subprocess.run` per file: definitive `private: true` -> True AND assert the observed call is `api repos/<ALERT_REPO>` carrying the ROUTE token; a public repo -> False; a failed lookup (rc != 0) -> False; unparseable/empty stdout -> False; a non-boolean `private` (e.g. the string "true", or 1) -> False. Keep the injected-lambda rows for the pure routing matrix - they are good - but they cannot substitute for exercising the live helper.
issues.title: Six new copies of the fail-closed `_repo_confirmed_private` helper ship with no direct assertions; its fail-closed branches are never executed

issues.body:
The `_alert_route` docstring is left unchanged: "the private ALERT_REPO only when ALERT_TOKEN is present; otherwise the registry repo under the ambient token."

After this diff, ALERT_TOKEN presence is no longer sufficient - the destination must additionally be distinct from the registry and be confirmed private by a live lookup. The stated sufficient condition is now wrong.

This matters more here than in an ordinary file because `_test_alert_route_contract` pins the docstring by EQUALITY against `canonical_route_doc` (line 574-577: "the router's docstring is EXACTLY the canonical contract"). The #1667 machinery that exists to keep this prose honest is now actively certifying a description that misstates a security control, and it will red on any attempt to correct the docstring alone.

The operational consequence is the part the prose no longer discloses: a maintainer who sets ALERT_REPO + ALERT_TOKEN will believe alerts land in the private repo, when a public ALERT_REPO, a token without repository-metadata read, or a transient API failure now silently redirects the alert body to the PUBLIC registry repo. Unlike groom-mint-alert.py, which carries an explicit PRIVACY paragraph concluding "the registry-repo fallback in _alert_route is safe", this file states no such justification for what its body may contain.
issues.fix_hint: Update `canonical_route_doc` and the live `_alert_route` docstring together in the same commit, following the wording already approved in groom-alert.py:61-76: state that ALERT_REPO is selected ONLY when the token is present, the repo is distinct from the registry (case-insensitive), AND the destination is CONFIRMED private by a live GET /repos/{ALERT_REPO}; that presence is configuration, not verification; and that every other shape falls back to the registry. Watch the `claims_about_the_route` phrasing list - the replacement must not reintroduce a write-capability claim such as "can write there". Add a one-line statement of what this body may contain, so the fallback-to-public path is a stated decision rather than an undocumented one.
issues.title: The governed-prose equality test now pins a router docstring that this PR made false

issues.body:
`_alert_route`'s docstring still reads "identical semantics to groom-alert/usage-alert: the private ALERT_REPO only when ALERT_TOKEN is present; otherwise the registry repo under the ambient token."

Both halves are now false. Presence is no longer sufficient (distinctness plus confirmed-private are required), and groom-alert.py:61-76 - the file cited as the reference - carries a materially different, updated contract, so the "identical semantics" claim points at prose that no longer matches.

As in park-stock-alert.py, this module's `_test_alert_route_contract` scans and pins the router's prose (see lines 992-998), so the stale text is now guarded rather than merely stale. The new behavioural rows added just below it (`#1775: ...`) assert the correct behaviour, which makes the mismatch between the pinned prose and the pinned behaviour visible in the same function.
issues.fix_hint: Rewrite the docstring to the groom-alert.py:61-76 contract and update whatever canonical/expected prose fixture this module's `_test_alert_route_contract` compares against, in the same commit. Keep the cross-file "identical semantics" reference only if it still resolves to matching text after the update; otherwise drop it rather than let it rot.
issues.title: Same stale pinned docstring: the router still documents the presence-only contract

issues.body:
dispatch-stall-alert.py, ci-latency-alert.py, groom-mint-alert.py and metrics-alert.py all retain the sentence "the private ALERT_REPO is the destination ONLY when ALERT_TOKEN can write there; a half-configured deployment (repo set, token missing) falls back to the registry repo".

That sentence describes the pre-diff behaviour. It omits both new preconditions (distinct-from-registry, confirmed-private) and, more importantly for a reader, omits the newly reachable outcome in which a fully-configured deployment still falls back to the public registry because the visibility probe did not return a definitive `private: true`. The half-configured case is no longer the only fallback.

These are also the docstrings that assert cross-file "identical semantics and signature" - a claim that is now the only written record of a contract none of them states correctly.
issues.fix_hint: Apply the groom-alert.py:61-76 wording to all four docstrings, including the explicit note that presence of both env vars is configuration rather than verification, and that an unconfirmed destination falls back to the registry.
issues.title: Router docstrings in four files still assert the presence-implies-capability contract

issues.body:
`_test_no_hold_labels` pins "the COMPLETE set of gh commands this module can construct" and the expected nouns move from `["issue", "label"]` to `["api", "issue", "label"]`.

The widening is necessary for the visibility probe, and the verb set is correctly left unchanged. But the assertion now admits ANY `_gh(["api", <f-string>])` call: the path is an f-string, so it is not an `ast.Constant` and is silently dropped from `words`, meaning nothing in the test constrains which endpoint may be reached. The guard's stated purpose ("no `pr`, no merge, no arming") still largely holds, since an explicit `"-X"` literal would land in `verbs` and red - but that is incidental, not asserted.

The same widening lands untested in the other five files, which have no equivalent structural census.
issues.fix_hint: Alongside the noun set, assert the shape of every `api` argv this module can construct - e.g. that each `_gh(["api", ...])` call site has exactly two elements, that the second is an f-string whose static prefix is `repos/`, and that no `-X`/`--method`/`-f`/`--input` literal appears in any `api` argv. That keeps the read-only intent of the new call statically readable, which is the property this test exists to preserve.
issues.title: Structural authority-surface test widened to admit the `api` noun without pinning the path or method

AGENTS.md:6-7 states that source-file provenance headers use the model-agnostic `[SPARQ agent]` marker and that model-qualified markers such as `[OPUS-5]` "are legacy and migrate when touched".

This PR correctly migrates groom-mint-alert.py and metrics-alert.py, but triage-stock-alert.py (also touched) keeps its `[OPUS-5]` header. The migration is applied inconsistently across the same diff.
issues.fix_hint: Migrate the `[OPUS-5]` header in triage-stock-alert.py to `[SPARQ agent]` for consistency with the two files already migrated in this diff, or drop the two header renames from this PR entirely and land them as a separate sweep.

verdict.summary:
The core change is right and in the fail-closed direction: the six new `_alert_route` bodies are byte-identical to the already-audited reference in scripts/groom-alert.py:77-82 (require ALERT_TOKEN, require ALERT_REPO distinct from the registry case-insensitively, require a positively confirmed `"private": true`, otherwise fall back to the registry under the ambient token). The three new pure-route rows per file are NOT vacuous: the `lambda r, t: False` row reds if the confirmation call is dropped, and the `calls.append(r) or True` probe reds if the same-repo short-circuit is removed or is made to consult the lookup. No token is echoed; the payload is parsed, not printed. The park-stock wiring test's `/pulls?` disambiguation correctly stops the new `repos/...` read from being mistaken for the PR census read.

What blocks approval is coverage and prose, both measured against this repo's own established bar rather than an invented one.

(1) `_repo_confirmed_private` is duplicated into six scripts with ZERO direct assertions in any of them. Every new self-test row injects a lambda, so the real helper's fail-closed branches (non-zero rc, unparseable JSON, `private: false`, non-boolean) are never executed. In ci-latency-alert.py, dispatch-stall-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py the helper is not executed at all; in the other three the gh fakes stub only the happy `private: true` path. Four sibling copies already in the tree (groom-alert.py:385-398, plan-alert.py:580-593, usage-alert.py:896-911, worker-pr.py:11886-11902) each pin five rows for exactly this helper. A copy slip such as truthy `payload.get("private")` instead of `is True`, or a dropped returncode check, would ship green.

(2) park-stock-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py still carry the presence-only router docstring, and park-stock's `_test_alert_route_contract` pins that docstring by EQUALITY (line 574-577). The governed-prose guard now certifies a contract this PR falsified.
